# A Novel Hyaluronic Acid Matrix Ingredient with Regenerative, Anti-Aging and Antioxidant Capacity

**Авторы:** Galvez-Martin Patricia, Soto-Fernandez Cristina, Romero-Rueda Jessica, Cabañas Jesus, Torrent Anna, Castells Gloria, Martinez-Puig Daniel

**Журнал:** International Journal of Molecular Sciences (2023)

**DOI:** 10.3390/ijms24054774


## Abstract

Hyaluronic acid (HA) and proteoglycans (such as dermatan sulphate (DS) and chondroitin sulphate (CS)) are the main components of the extracellular matrix of the skin, along with collagen and elastin.
source_units.reason: article_metadata_header

source_units.text: These components decrease with age, which implies a loss of skin moisture causing wrinkles, sagging and aging.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Currently, the external and internal administration of effective ingredients that can reach the epidermis and dermis is the main alternative for combating skin aging.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The objective of this work was to extract, characterise and evaluate the potential of an HA matrix ingredient to support anti-aging.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The HA matrix was isolated and purified from rooster comb and characterised physicochemically and molecularly.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In addition, its regenerative, anti-aging and antioxidant potential and intestinal absorption were evaluated.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The results show that the HA matrix is composed of 67% HA, with an average molecular weight of 1.3 MDa; 12% sulphated glycosaminoglycans, including DS and CS; 17% protein, including collagen (10.4%); and water.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The in vitro evaluation of the HA matrix’s biological activity showed regenerative properties in both fibroblasts and keratinocytes, as well as moisturising, anti-aging and antioxidant effects.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Furthermore, the results suggest that the HA matrix could be absorbed in the intestine, implying a potential oral as well as topical use for skin care, either as an ingredient in a nutraceutical or a cosmetic product.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
Introduction

The skin is the largest organ of the body, representing one-sixth of the total body weight with an approximate surface area of 1.5–2 m [1,2].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Its primary role is to provide a physical barrier to protect internal tissues from the external environment and it is, therefore, constantly exposed to mechanical and chemical threats, temperature changes, pathogens, ultraviolet radiation and dehydration [3].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The skin consists of three layers called the epidermis, dermis and hypodermis, each with different structures and compositions (Figure 1). The epidermis is the most superficial layer whose function is to prevent both water loss from the body and penetration of pathogens from the environment. Structurally, the epidermis is made up of dense cell layers, mainly keratinocytes, which synthesise keratin, phospholipids and sphingolipids and critically contribute to the barrier function [4].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In contrast, fibroblasts are the most abundant cells in the dermis.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: They are responsible for synthesising and remodelling a complex extracellular matrix (ECM) containing collagen, elastin and glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) [5].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Collagen fibres make up about 75% of the dry weight of the skin and they provide tensile strength [6], while elastin forms a network with collagen fibres and provides elasticity [5].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: GAGs, mainly composed of hyaluronic acid (HA), dermatan sulphate (DS) and chondroitin sulphate (CS), have both structural and signalling roles.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Structurally, GAGs help maintain skin hydration, and from a signalling perspective, they regulate cell migration, proliferation and differentiation, as well as ECM homeostasis [7].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In addition, their potential to moderate cytokines and antioxidant status in animals has been described [8].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Below the dermis, the hypodermis is composed of adipose and connective tissue and provides insulation from heat and cold [9].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Abbreviations: UV (ultraviolet); ROS (reactive oxygen species); MMP (metalloproteinases); HA (hyaluronic acid); ECMp (extracellular matrix proteins); Col (collagen); GAGs (glycosaminoglycans). With the aging process, the structure and composition of the skin change as a result of environmental threats, such as ultraviolet exposure, air pollution and tobacco smoke, among others (extrinsic factors), as well as biological aging (intrinsic factors) [10].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Oxidative stress also contributes to both intrinsic and extrinsic skin aging [11].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) produced as a result of ultraviolet exposure or metabolically generated increase the expression of metalloproteinases (MMPs) that degrade ECM proteins (ECMp) [12].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: MMP levels are elevated in aged or photodamaged skin [13].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: MMP-1 is the primary protease responsible for the fragmentation of type I and type III collagen, which are predominant in human skin [14], whereas MMP-12 is the most active in the degradation of elastin [15].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: As a result of increased MMPs activity, collagen and elastin fibres are degraded and disorganised in aged skin.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The increased degradation coupled with reduced biosynthesis results in a net collagen and elastin deficiency [16,17].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In terms of GAGs, deficiencies of HA and total sulphated GAGs have also been documented as a result of the aging process.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Both intrinsic and extrinsic factors appear to downregulate HA synthases, resulting in a reduction of HA levels, particularly in the epidermis [18].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The reduction in the molecular weight (MW) of HA has been suggested to be mediated by ROS [19].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In parallel with HA, levels of total sulphated GAGs have been shown to be reduced in aged skin compared to young skin [20].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Thus, the aging process is associated with a reduction of epidermal and dermal thickness and quality [21], resulting in the appearance of fine wrinkles and flaccid, dry and dull skin (Figure 1).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Given the increasingly serious aging trend in today’s society, as well as the significant social burden and research investment, it is of great social and scientific significance to strengthen the development of anti-aging products.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The most effective way to combat visible signs of skin aging and improve its appearance and quality is to provide effective ingredients that can reach the epidermis and dermis, both externally and internally, and inhibit the main mechanisms associated with aging [22,23].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: HA is one of the most widely used biomolecules to treat skin aging.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: There are different sources of HA, such as microbial fermentation (F-HA) and extraction from mammalian and marine animals (E-HA).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Both origins are the most standardized due to their high performance and optimization of the processes for obtaining them, during which the intrinsic properties of HA must be maintained.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: More recently, cell-free systems are being studied as a new source of HA, but these still present some process limitations and cannot yet be used for industrial production [24].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The process of obtaining HA mainly involves two phases: the extraction phase and the purification phase.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The extraction phase of F-HA is carried out from the culture medium of bacterial strains (e.g., Streptococci, Bacilli and Escherichia coli) [25].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Then, the culture medium is ultrafiltered.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Regarding the E-HA, it can be obtained mainly from tissues such as rooster comb, umbilical cord, vitreous humour and synovial liquid through a process of mechanical crushing and delipidation with ethanol [26,27].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Then, different procedures can be performed to continue with the extraction process of HA: the extraction method with hot water or with a diluted alkali–water solution (e.g., NaOH solution or NaCO3 solution) or through an enzymatic hydrolysis (using enzymes such as papain or alcalasa) [28].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Finally, F-HA and E-HA are purified by precipitation using organic solvents (acetic acid or ethanol), neutral salts (NaCl, KCl), metal ions (copper, calcium), quaternary ammonium salts of long chain (cetyl trimethyl ammonium bromide, cetylpyridinium chloride) or through the column chromatography method with a cellulose column, an anion exchange column or a gel column [24,29].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Based on the origin and the obtaining process of HA, its efficacy and safety can vary enormously [30,31].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This implies the need to evaluate the safety and efficacy of HA-based products in both in vitro and in vivo studies.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The aim of this study was to assess the anti-aging properties of an HA matrix ingredient containing a high concentration of HA, sulphated GAGs (specifically CS/DS) and collagen.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To achieve this, we first extracted the HA matrix ingredient from rooster comb and its physicochemical characterisation was performed.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Then, its regenerative, anti-aging and antioxidant properties were tested in vitro and finally, its intestinal absorption was evaluated.

### 2.3. HA Matrix Effects on Skin Cell Viability
